statements.attributed: oxygen-deficient CeO2−δ polymorphs can be formed upon oxygen loss
statements.quote: Various oxygen-deficient CeO2−δ polymorphs within the Ce2O3–CeO2 composition range can be formed upon oxygen loss. Frenkel-type oxygen defects, which involve displacement of oxygen atoms from the octahedral interstitial sites in the fluorite lattice, are also common in CeO2. Discerning these stoichiometric and nonstoichiometric oxygen defects on the surface and in the bulk of ceria-based HEOs is thus challenging yet crucial, particularly for nanocatalysis.

statements.attributed: pronounced local structural heterogeneities involving distinct surface and bulk domains of HEOs
statements.quote: Recent studies have observed pronounced local structural heterogeneities involving distinct surface and bulk domains of HEOs during synthesis and catalysis processes. Instead of the formation of entropy-stabilized single-phase solid solutions, building surface-confined HEO domains provides an alternative to tailor the surface reactivities of ceria via oxygen defect engineering.

statements.attributed: UV Raman spectra can probe the dynamic interaction between the metal and oxygen atoms in ceria
statements.quote: Figure 2e displays the ultraviolet (UV) Raman spectra of the annealed CeO2 samples measured with a 325 nm excitation wavelength, which probes the dynamic interaction between the metal and oxygen atoms in ceria with a strong resonance effect. CeO2 exhibits the characteristic F2g and defect-induced D modes at 467 and 599 cm–1, respectively, together with the 2LO mode centered at 1188 cm–1.

statements.attributed: neutron diffraction can identify the positions of the oxygen atoms in the transition-metal-substituted CeO2 nanocrystals
statements.quote: Neutron diffraction, which relies on short-range nuclear interactions and thus possesses a high detection sensitivity for light elements, was employed to identify the positions of the oxygen atoms in the transition-metal-substituted CeO2 nanocrystals.

statements.attributed: a minor rock salt, sub-nanometer HEO phase emerged for CuCoFeNiMn-CeO2
statements.quote: According to the Rietveld refinements (Figures S11–S14 and Table S6), no (crystalline) impurity phase was observed for CeO2, Cu-CeO2, and CuCo-CeO2, whereas a minor rock salt, sub-nanometer (<5 Å) HEO phase emerged for CuCoFeNiMn-CeO2. Moreover, no substantial changes were observed for the refined lattice parameters of CeO2 among these four samples.

statements.quote: Following the Mars–van Krevelen mechanism, CO molecules are adsorbed and oxidized by the activated lattice oxygen on the CeO2 surface, where the accompanying oxygen vacancies are repeatedly filled by the dissociated oxygen molecules in the atmosphere.

While the position of the first peak remains at ∼100 °C, the second peak observably shifts toward lower temperatures for CuCo-CeO2 (216 °C) and CuCoFeNiMn-CeO2 (179 °C).
